brief.product: An AI executive assistant for one person. It reads their mail and calendar, writes a morning briefing, drafts replies, remembers people and commitments, and asks for approval before anything leaves with their name on it. Used all day by a busy executive or founder, in short glances between meetings rather than long sessions, plus an admin view for the person running the platform.
brief.notes: Most of the product happens in the background, so screens are mostly reading surfaces: a stat row, lists with counts, a chat panel beside a page being read. Amber is reserved for "this wants you" (Needs you rows, a drafted reply waiting, new chat bubbles) and must stay distinct from the accent. Dark mode is used a lot; muted text needs 4.5:1 measured against the dark surface, not eyeballed. Icons are Heroicons only, no Lucide mixing. It should feel like a quiet, competent assistant, not a dashboard and not a bank.

accent.why: A muted indigo sits roughly opposite the amber the brief reserves for 'this wants you', so the two never compete, and it avoids the navy that banks and dashboards lean on.

temperature.why: Slate greys suit a software assistant and give the dark register the brief says is used a lot a calm, even surface for long reading.

pairing.why: A morning briefing and drafted replies are read like an authored note, and Newsreader at title size gives that feel while Hanken Grotesk stays quiet in the lists and chat.

radius.why: The brief wants neither the sharp edges of a data tool nor the rounded feel of a consumer app, so the default step fits.

density.why: The executive uses it in short glances between meetings rather than working the screens all day as trained staff, so the larger spacing helps them find things fast.

motif.why: A thin bar marks the active item and selected row without filling anything, which keeps the accent quiet and leaves amber as the only colour that asks for attention in a row.

copy.headline: Your morning, already read.
copy.tagline: Sign in to see what came in overnight and what needs your word.
copy.why: It speaks to what the executive opens the app to do, catch up and approve, without describing the assistant or its features.
